title: Global Identification of the Average Treatment Effect in Binary Proximal Models
banked_reason: Delivered tier incremental below field floor; mathematically sound after D0.5 rerun, with unresolved comparator and prior-art positioning caveats.
gap_reasons: Delivered tier incremental < floor field; not salvageable within scope.
The ATE gap requires an entirely absent treatment arm and externally declared, unequal deterministic responses for that unobserved arm, limiting its econometric reach.
The comparisons with bridge-solution null spaces and tensor identification criteria remain qualitative rather than a direct evaluation on common faces or laws.
Guo--Ogburn--Shpitser, arXiv:2512.00175v2, §3.1, Theorem 3.5 is Kruskal's general CP-uniqueness theorem, not an armwise recovery condition.
Duan et al. (2020), abstract and introduction, is already listed but is not positioned: it explicitly contrasts local and global latent-class identifiability via Gröbner methods.
proof_attempt_summary: The D0 derivation proved a local-to-global ATE classification and an exact two-candidate set for full-rank absent-arm fixed-bit faces, including a rational witness. A scoped D0 correction cleared all mathematical reviewer findings on the D0.5 rerun. The result remained incremental below the required field floor; a broader all-face sharp-set program and literature positioning remain for a future re-anchor.
tldr: On a fixed declared binary two-class face, feasible-tangent nullity forces a globally constant ATE whenever both treatment arms occur or the observational tensor is deficient. For an absent arm with fixed missing-response bits and full-rank factual \(Y,Z,W\) columns, an explicit moment reconstruction and primitive-tag filter \(I_F\) give the sharp identified set. Under tangent nullity, a gap occurs exactly on the full-support, distinct-bit, nonzero-\(\kappa\) branch. The rational witness has two isolated, non-label-equivalent completions with different ATEs.
gap: Bridge null-space criteria concern affine bridge equations, while tensor uniqueness recovers observational components. Neither determines how declared off-treatment response bits attach to components of a nonlinear primitive causal fiber.
fill: Prove a precise local-to-global boundary, classify deficient fibers, and certify the only proposed regular failure by exact causal twins and observable moments.
